func (c *LRUCache) estimateMemoryUsage() int64 {
        // Rough estimation:
        // - Each entry has repository object overhead (~1KB)
        // - Git repo objects are harder to estimate, use conservative 10KB average
        // - Repository metadata ~500 bytes
        // This is a simplified estimation for monitoring purposes
        const avgRepoSize = 11 * 1024 // 11KB per repository (conservative estimate)

        metrics := c.GetMetrics()
        return metrics.Entries * avgRepoSize
}

// estimateMemoryUsageWithEntries provides memory estimate with given entry count
// This version is used internally when we already have the entry count to avoid recursive locking
func (c *LRUCache) estimateMemoryUsageWithEntries(entries int64) int64 {
        const avgRepoSize = 11 * 1024 // 11KB per repository (conservative estimate)
        return entries * avgRepoSize
}

// RepositoryCache interface implementation

// GetRepository retrieves a cached repository by its filesystem path.
// Returns the repository and true if found, or nil and false if not cached.
func (c *LRUCache) GetRepository(path string) (*gogit.Repository, bool) {
        // Use the existing Get method
        repo, exists := c.Get(path)
        if !exists || repo == nil {
                return nil, false
        }

        // Extract the git repository from our Repository wrapper
        return repo.GitRepo, true
}

// SetRepository stores a repository in the cache with its filesystem path as the key.
// The cache implementation handles eviction according to its policy.
func (c *LRUCache) SetRepository(path string, repo *gogit.Repository) error {
        // Use the existing Set method which handles the Repository wrapper creation
        return c.Set(path, repo)
}

// InvalidateRepository removes a repository from the cache.
// This should be called when a repository is modified (e.g., after a push).
func (c *LRUCache) InvalidateRepository(path string) bool {
        c.mutex.Lock()
        defer c.mutex.Unlock()

        if !c.config.Enabled {
                return false
        }

        // Check if it exists
        if _, exists := c.cache.Get(path); !exists {
                return false
        }

        // Remove from cache
        removed := c.cache.Remove(path)
        if removed {
                c.decrementEntries()
        }

        return removed
}

// InvalidateAll removes all repositories from the cache.
// Useful for cache maintenance or when global repository changes occur.
func (c *LRUCache) InvalidateAll() {
        // Use the existing Purge method
        c.Purge()
}

// Ensure LRUCache implements RepositoryCache interface
var _ RepositoryCache = (*LRUCache)(nil)

package cache

import (
        "sync"

        "github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
        "github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promauto"
        dto "github.com/prometheus/client_model/go"
)

// Global singleton for default prometheus metrics to avoid duplicate registrations
var (
        defaultPrometheusMetrics *PrometheusMetrics
        defaultMetricsOnce       sync.Once
)

// PrometheusMetrics holds all Prometheus metrics for the cache
type PrometheusMetrics struct {
        // Counter metrics for tracking cache operations
        CacheHitsTotal      prometheus.Counter
        CacheMissesTotal    prometheus.Counter
        CacheEvictionsTotal prometheus.Counter

        // Gauge metrics for current state
        CacheEntriesCurrent prometheus.Gauge
        CacheMemoryBytes    prometheus.Gauge

        // Additional detailed metrics
        CacheOperationsTotal prometheus.CounterVec   // labeled by operation type
        CacheAccessDuration  prometheus.HistogramVec // cache access latency
}

// NewPrometheusMetrics creates and registers all Prometheus metrics for cache monitoring
// This uses a singleton pattern to avoid duplicate registrations with the default registry
func NewPrometheusMetrics() *PrometheusMetrics {
        defaultMetricsOnce.Do(func() {
                defaultPrometheusMetrics = &PrometheusMetrics{
                        // Basic cache operation counters
                        CacheHitsTotal: promauto.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
                                Name: "cache_hits_total",
                                Help: "Total number of cache hits",
                        }),

                        CacheMissesTotal: promauto.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
                                Name: "cache_misses_total",
                                Help: "Total number of cache misses",
                        }),

                        CacheEvictionsTotal: promauto.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
                                Name: "cache_evictions_total",
                                Help: "Total number of cache evictions",
                        }),

                        // Current state gauges
                        CacheEntriesCurrent: promauto.NewGauge(prometheus.GaugeOpts{
                                Name: "cache_entries_current",
                                Help: "Current number of entries in the cache",
                        }),

                        CacheMemoryBytes: promauto.NewGauge(prometheus.GaugeOpts{
                                Name: "cache_memory_bytes",
                                Help: "Estimated memory usage of the cache in bytes",
                        }),

                        // Detailed operation metrics
                        CacheOperationsTotal: *promauto.NewCounterVec(
                                prometheus.CounterOpts{
                                        Name: "cache_operations_total",
                                        Help: "Total number of cache operations by type",
                                },
                                []string{"operation"}, // labels: get, set, evict, cleanup
                        ),

                        // Performance metrics
                        CacheAccessDuration: *promauto.NewHistogramVec(
                                prometheus.HistogramOpts{
                                        Name:    "cache_access_duration_seconds",
                                        Help:    "Duration of cache access operations",
                                        Buckets: prometheus.DefBuckets,
                                },
                                []string{"operation", "result"}, // operation: get/set, result: hit/miss/success
                        ),
                }
        })
        return defaultPrometheusMetrics
}

// NewPrometheusMetricsWithRegistry creates metrics with a custom registry (useful for testing)
func NewPrometheusMetricsWithRegistry(registry prometheus.Registerer) *PrometheusMetrics {
        return &PrometheusMetrics{
                CacheHitsTotal: prometheus.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
                        Name: "cache_hits_total",
                        Help: "Total number of cache hits",
                }),

                CacheMissesTotal: prometheus.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
                        Name: "cache_misses_total",
                        Help: "Total number of cache misses",
                }),

                CacheEvictionsTotal: prometheus.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
                        Name: "cache_evictions_total",
                        Help: "Total number of cache evictions",
                }),

                CacheEntriesCurrent: prometheus.NewGauge(prometheus.GaugeOpts{
                        Name: "cache_entries_current",
                        Help: "Current number of entries in the cache",
                }),

                CacheMemoryBytes: prometheus.NewGauge(prometheus.GaugeOpts{
                        Name: "cache_memory_bytes",
                        Help: "Estimated memory usage of the cache in bytes",
                }),

                CacheOperationsTotal: *prometheus.NewCounterVec(
                        prometheus.CounterOpts{
                                Name: "cache_operations_total",
                                Help: "Total number of cache operations by type",
                        },
                        []string{"operation"},
                ),

                CacheAccessDuration: *prometheus.NewHistogramVec(
                        prometheus.HistogramOpts{
                                Name:    "cache_access_duration_seconds",
                                Help:    "Duration of cache access operations",
                                Buckets: prometheus.DefBuckets,
                        },
                        []string{"operation", "result"},
                ),
        }
}

// RegisterMetrics registers all metrics with the provided registry
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RegisterMetrics(registry prometheus.Registerer) error {
        collectors := []prometheus.Collector{
                m.CacheHitsTotal,
                m.CacheMissesTotal,
                m.CacheEvictionsTotal,
                m.CacheEntriesCurrent,
                m.CacheMemoryBytes,
                &m.CacheOperationsTotal,
                &m.CacheAccessDuration,
        }

        for _, collector := range collectors {
                if err := registry.Register(collector); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }

        return nil
}

// RecordHit records a cache hit
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RecordHit() {
        m.CacheHitsTotal.Inc()
        m.CacheOperationsTotal.WithLabelValues("get").Inc()
}

// RecordMiss records a cache miss
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RecordMiss() {
        m.CacheMissesTotal.Inc()
        m.CacheOperationsTotal.WithLabelValues("get").Inc()
}

// RecordEviction records a cache eviction
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RecordEviction() {
        m.CacheEvictionsTotal.Inc()
        m.CacheOperationsTotal.WithLabelValues("evict").Inc()
}

// RecordSet records a cache set operation
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RecordSet() {
        m.CacheOperationsTotal.WithLabelValues("set").Inc()
}

// RecordCleanup records a cleanup operation
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RecordCleanup() {
        m.CacheOperationsTotal.WithLabelValues("cleanup").Inc()
}

// UpdateEntries updates the current number of cache entries
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) UpdateEntries(count int64) {
        m.CacheEntriesCurrent.Set(float64(count))
}

// UpdateMemoryUsage updates the estimated memory usage
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) UpdateMemoryUsage(bytes int64) {
        m.CacheMemoryBytes.Set(float64(bytes))
}

// RecordAccessDuration records the duration of a cache access operation
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) RecordAccessDuration(operation, result string, duration float64) {
        m.CacheAccessDuration.WithLabelValues(operation, result).Observe(duration)
}

// GetHitRate calculates and returns the current cache hit rate
func (m *PrometheusMetrics) GetHitRate() float64 {
        hits := getCounterValue(m.CacheHitsTotal)
        misses := getCounterValue(m.CacheMissesTotal)
        total := hits + misses

        if total == 0 {
                return 0.0
        }

        return hits / total
}

// Helper function to get counter value (for testing and monitoring)
func getCounterValue(counter prometheus.Counter) float64 {
        pb := &dto.Metric{}
        if err := counter.Write(pb); err != nil {
                return 0
        }
        return pb.GetCounter().GetValue()
}

package config

import (
        "fmt"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"

        "github.com/spf13/viper"
)

// Config represents the complete application configuration
type Config struct {
        Server  ServerConfig  `mapstructure:"server" validate:"required"`
        Git     GitConfig     `mapstructure:"git" validate:"required"`
        JWT     JWTConfig     `mapstructure:"jwt" validate:"required"`
        Logging LoggingConfig `mapstructure:"logging"`
        mu      sync.RWMutex
}

// ServerConfig holds HTTP server configuration
type ServerConfig struct {
        Port            int           `mapstructure:"port" validate:"required,min=1,max=65535"`
        BasePath        string        `mapstructure:"base_path" validate:"required"`
        Host            string        `mapstructure:"host"`
        ReadTimeout     time.Duration `mapstructure:"read_timeout"`
        WriteTimeout    time.Duration `mapstructure:"write_timeout"`
        IdleTimeout     time.Duration `mapstructure:"idle_timeout"`
        ShutdownTimeout time.Duration `mapstructure:"shutdown_timeout"`
        HealthCheckPath string        `mapstructure:"health_check_path"`
}

// GitConfig holds Git repository configuration
type GitConfig struct {
        RepoRoot       string        `mapstructure:"repo_root" validate:"required"`
        EnablePackfile bool          `mapstructure:"enable_packfile"`
        MaxCacheSize   int           `mapstructure:"max_cache_size"`
        CacheTTL       time.Duration `mapstructure:"cache_ttl"`
}

// JWTConfig holds JWT authentication configuration
type JWTConfig struct {
        Algorithm     string `mapstructure:"algorithm" validate:"required,oneof=RS256 HS256 ES256"`
        PublicKeyPath string `mapstructure:"public_key_path"`
        SecretKey     string `mapstructure:"secret_key"`
}

// LoggingConfig holds logging configuration
type LoggingConfig struct {
        Level       string `mapstructure:"level"`
        Format      string `mapstructure:"format"`
        Output      string `mapstructure:"output"`
        Development bool   `mapstructure:"development"`
}

// Load loads configuration from file with Viper
func Load(configPath string) (*Config, error) {
        // Reset Viper to ensure clean state
        viper.Reset()

        // Set defaults first
        setDefaults()

        // Configure Viper
        viper.SetConfigType("yaml")
        viper.SetConfigName("config")

        if configPath != "" {
                viper.SetConfigFile(configPath)
        } else {
                // Add config search paths
                viper.AddConfigPath("./config")
                viper.AddConfigPath(".")
                viper.AddConfigPath("/etc/collabops")
        }

        // Enable environment variable support
        viper.SetEnvPrefix("COLLABOPS")
        viper.SetEnvKeyReplacer(strings.NewReplacer(".", "_"))
        viper.AutomaticEnv()

        // Read configuration file
        if err := viper.ReadInConfig(); err != nil {
                if _, ok := err.(viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError); ok {
                        // Config file not found; use defaults
                        // Note: Can't use logger here as it's not initialized yet
                } else if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no such file or directory") {
                        // Specific file path doesn't exist; use defaults
                        // Note: Can't use logger here as it's not initialized yet
                } else {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read config file: %w", err)
                }
        }

        // Unmarshal configuration
        var config Config
        if err := viper.Unmarshal(&config); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal config: %w", err)
        }

        // Validate configuration
        if err := validate(&config); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("config validation failed: %w", err)
        }

        return &config, nil
}

// setDefaults sets default configuration values
func setDefaults() {
        // Server defaults
        viper.SetDefault("server.port", 8080)
        viper.SetDefault("server.base_path", "/repos")
        viper.SetDefault("server.host", "0.0.0.0")
        viper.SetDefault("server.read_timeout", "30s")
        viper.SetDefault("server.write_timeout", "30s")
        viper.SetDefault("server.idle_timeout", "120s")

        // Git defaults
        viper.SetDefault("git.repo_root", "/var/lib/git/repos")
        viper.SetDefault("git.enable_packfile", true)
        viper.SetDefault("git.max_cache_size", 100)
        viper.SetDefault("git.cache_ttl", "5m")

        // JWT defaults
        viper.SetDefault("jwt.algorithm", "RS256")
        viper.SetDefault("jwt.public_key_path", "/etc/collabops/public.pem")

        // Server additional defaults
        viper.SetDefault("server.shutdown_timeout", "30s")
        viper.SetDefault("server.health_check_path", "/health")

        // Logging defaults
        viper.SetDefault("logging.level", "info")
        viper.SetDefault("logging.format", "json")
        viper.SetDefault("logging.output", "stdout")
        viper.SetDefault("logging.development", false)
}

// validate performs configuration validation
func validate(config *Config) error {
        var errors []string

        // Validate server configuration
        if config.Server.Port < 1 || config.Server.Port > 65535 {
                errors = append(errors, "server.port must be between 1 and 65535")
        }

        if config.Server.BasePath == "" {
                errors = append(errors, "server.base_path is required")
        }

        if !strings.HasPrefix(config.Server.BasePath, "/") {
                errors = append(errors, "server.base_path must start with '/'")
        }

        // Validate Git configuration
        if config.Git.RepoRoot == "" {
                errors = append(errors, "git.repo_root is required")
        }

        if config.Git.MaxCacheSize < 0 {
                errors = append(errors, "git.max_cache_size must be >= 0")
        }

        // Validate JWT configuration
        validAlgorithms := []string{"RS256", "HS256", "ES256"}
        algorithmValid := false
        for _, alg := range validAlgorithms {
                if config.JWT.Algorithm == alg {
                        algorithmValid = true
                        break
                }
        }
        if !algorithmValid {
                errors = append(errors, fmt.Sprintf("jwt.algorithm must be one of: %v", validAlgorithms))
        }

        // For RS256 and ES256, public key path is required
        if (config.JWT.Algorithm == "RS256" || config.JWT.Algorithm == "ES256") && config.JWT.PublicKeyPath == "" {
                errors = append(errors, fmt.Sprintf("jwt.public_key_path is required for algorithm %s", config.JWT.Algorithm))
        }

        // For HS256, secret key is required
        if config.JWT.Algorithm == "HS256" && config.JWT.SecretKey == "" {
                errors = append(errors, "jwt.secret_key is required for algorithm HS256")
        }

        // Validate logging configuration
        validLogLevels := []string{"debug", "info", "warn", "error", "fatal"}
        logLevelValid := false
        for _, level := range validLogLevels {
                if config.Logging.Level == level {
                        logLevelValid = true
                        break
                }
        }
        if !logLevelValid {
                errors = append(errors, fmt.Sprintf("logging.level must be one of: %v", validLogLevels))
        }

        validLogFormats := []string{"json", "text"}
        logFormatValid := false
        for _, format := range validLogFormats {
                if config.Logging.Format == format {
                        logFormatValid = true
                        break
                }
        }
        if !logFormatValid {
                errors = append(errors, fmt.Sprintf("logging.format must be one of: %v", validLogFormats))
        }

        if len(errors) > 0 {
                return fmt.Errorf("validation errors: %s", strings.Join(errors, "; "))
        }

        return nil
}

// GetConfigPath returns the path to the configuration file being used
func GetConfigPath() string {
        return viper.ConfigFileUsed()
}

// GetServer returns a copy of the server configuration (thread-safe)
func (c *Config) GetServer() ServerConfig {
        c.mu.RLock()
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()
        return c.Server
}

// GetGit returns a copy of the git configuration (thread-safe)
func (c *Config) GetGit() GitConfig {
        c.mu.RLock()
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()
        return c.Git
}

// GetJWT returns a copy of the JWT configuration (thread-safe)
func (c *Config) GetJWT() JWTConfig {
        c.mu.RLock()
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()
        return c.JWT
}

// GetLogging returns a copy of the logging configuration (thread-safe)
func (c *Config) GetLogging() LoggingConfig {
        c.mu.RLock()
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()
        return c.Logging
}

// Reload reloads the configuration from file (thread-safe)
func (c *Config) Reload() error {
        c.mu.Lock()
        defer c.mu.Unlock()

        // Re-read configuration
        if err := viper.ReadInConfig(); err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("failed to reload config: %w", err)
        }

        // Create temporary config to validate
        var newConfig Config
        if err := viper.Unmarshal(&newConfig); err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmarshal reloaded config: %w", err)
        }

        // Validate new configuration
        if err := validate(&newConfig); err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("reloaded config validation failed: %w", err)
        }

        // Update fields
        c.Server = newConfig.Server
        c.Git = newConfig.Git
        c.JWT = newConfig.JWT
        c.Logging = newConfig.Logging

        return nil
}

package git

import (
        "container/list"
        "sync"
        "time"
)

// RepositoryCache manages cached Repository instances with LRU eviction
type RepositoryCache struct {
        mu      sync.RWMutex
        items   map[string]*cacheItem
        lruList *list.List
        maxSize int
        maxAge  time.Duration
        onEvict func(path string, repo Repository)
}

// cacheItem represents a cached repository with metadata
type cacheItem struct {
        path      string
        repo      Repository
        createdAt time.Time
        lastUsed  time.Time
        element   *list.Element
}

// CacheConfig holds configuration for the repository cache
type CacheConfig struct {
        // MaxSize is the maximum number of repositories to cache (0 for unlimited)
        MaxSize int

        // MaxAge is the maximum age of cached repositories (0 for no expiration)
        MaxAge time.Duration

        // OnEvict is called when a repository is evicted from the cache
        OnEvict func(path string, repo Repository)
}

// DefaultCacheConfig returns a default cache configuration
func DefaultCacheConfig() *CacheConfig {
        return &CacheConfig{
                MaxSize: 100,              // Cache up to 100 repositories
                MaxAge:  30 * time.Minute, // Expire after 30 minutes
                OnEvict: func(path string, repo Repository) {
                        // Default eviction handler closes the repository
                        if repo != nil {
                                _ = repo.Close()
                        }
                },
        }
}

// NewRepositoryCache creates a new repository cache with the given configuration
func NewRepositoryCache(config *CacheConfig) *RepositoryCache {
        if config == nil {
                config = DefaultCacheConfig()
        }

        return &RepositoryCache{
                items:   make(map[string]*cacheItem),
                lruList: list.New(),
                maxSize: config.MaxSize,
                maxAge:  config.MaxAge,
                onEvict: config.OnEvict,
        }
}

// Get retrieves a repository from the cache
func (c *RepositoryCache) Get(path string) (Repository, bool) {
        c.mu.Lock()
        defer c.mu.Unlock()

        item, exists := c.items[path]
        if !exists {
                return nil, false
        }

        // Check if item has expired
        if c.maxAge > 0 && time.Since(item.createdAt) > c.maxAge {
                c.removeItem(item)
                return nil, false
        }

        // Update last used time and move to front of LRU list
        item.lastUsed = time.Now()
        c.lruList.MoveToFront(item.element)

        return item.repo, true
}

// Put stores a repository in the cache
func (c *RepositoryCache) Put(path string, repo Repository) {
        c.mu.Lock()
        defer c.mu.Unlock()

        // If item already exists, update it
        if existing, exists := c.items[path]; exists {
                existing.repo = repo
                existing.lastUsed = time.Now()
                existing.createdAt = time.Now()
                c.lruList.MoveToFront(existing.element)
                return
        }

        // Create new cache item
        now := time.Now()
        item := &cacheItem{
                path:      path,
                repo:      repo,
                createdAt: now,
                lastUsed:  now,
        }

        // Add to front of LRU list
        item.element = c.lruList.PushFront(item)
        c.items[path] = item

        // Evict oldest items if cache is full
        c.evictIfNeeded()
}

// Remove removes a repository from the cache
func (c *RepositoryCache) Remove(path string) bool {
        c.mu.Lock()
        defer c.mu.Unlock()

        item, exists := c.items[path]
        if !exists {
                return false
        }

        c.removeItem(item)
        return true
}

// Clear removes all repositories from the cache
func (c *RepositoryCache) Clear() {
        c.mu.Lock()
        defer c.mu.Unlock()

        // Call eviction callback for all items
        for _, item := range c.items {
                if c.onEvict != nil {
                        c.onEvict(item.path, item.repo)
                }
        }

        // Clear all data structures
        c.items = make(map[string]*cacheItem)
        c.lruList.Init()
}

// Size returns the current number of cached repositories
func (c *RepositoryCache) Size() int {
        c.mu.RLock()
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()
        return len(c.items)
}

// Stats returns cache statistics
func (c *RepositoryCache) Stats() CacheStats {
        c.mu.RLock()
        defer c.mu.RUnlock()

        stats := CacheStats{
                Size:    len(c.items),
                MaxSize: c.maxSize,
                MaxAge:  c.maxAge,
        }

        // Calculate oldest and newest items
        if len(c.items) > 0 {
                now := time.Now()
                oldest := now
                newest := time.Time{}

                for _, item := range c.items {
                        if item.createdAt.Before(oldest) {
                                oldest = item.createdAt
                        }
                        if item.createdAt.After(newest) {
                                newest = item.createdAt
                        }
                }

                stats.OldestAge = now.Sub(oldest)
                stats.NewestAge = now.Sub(newest)
        }

        return stats
}

// CleanupExpired removes all expired items from the cache
func (c *RepositoryCache) CleanupExpired() int {
        if c.maxAge <= 0 {
                return 0 // No expiration configured
        }

        c.mu.Lock()
        defer c.mu.Unlock()

        var expiredItems []*cacheItem
        cutoff := time.Now().Add(-c.maxAge)

        // Find expired items
        for _, item := range c.items {
                if item.createdAt.Before(cutoff) {
                        expiredItems = append(expiredItems, item)
                }
        }

        // Remove expired items
        for _, item := range expiredItems {
                c.removeItem(item)
        }

        return len(expiredItems)
}

// removeItem removes an item from the cache (must be called with lock held)
func (c *RepositoryCache) removeItem(item *cacheItem) {
        // Remove from map
        delete(c.items, item.path)

        // Remove from LRU list
        c.lruList.Remove(item.element)

        // Call eviction callback
        if c.onEvict != nil {
                c.onEvict(item.path, item.repo)
        }
}

// evictIfNeeded evicts oldest items if cache size exceeds maximum (must be called with lock held)
func (c *RepositoryCache) evictIfNeeded() {
        if c.maxSize <= 0 {
                return // No size limit configured
        }

        // Evict oldest items until we're under the size limit
        for len(c.items) > c.maxSize {
                // Get oldest item from back of LRU list
                oldest := c.lruList.Back()
                if oldest == nil {
                        break
                }

                item := oldest.Value.(*cacheItem)
                c.removeItem(item)
        }
}

// CacheStats provides statistics about the cache
type CacheStats struct {
        Size      int           `json:"size"`
        MaxSize   int           `json:"max_size"`
        MaxAge    time.Duration `json:"max_age"`
        OldestAge time.Duration `json:"oldest_age"`
        NewestAge time.Duration `json:"newest_age"`
}

// Global cache instance (can be overridden for testing)
var globalCache = NewRepositoryCache(DefaultCacheConfig())

// SetGlobalCache sets the global repository cache instance
func SetGlobalCache(cache *RepositoryCache) {
        globalCache = cache
}

// GetGlobalCache returns the global repository cache instance
func GetGlobalCache() *RepositoryCache {
        return globalCache
}

// ClearGlobalCache clears the global repository cache
func ClearGlobalCache() {
        globalCache.Clear()
}

// GetGlobalCacheStats returns statistics for the global cache
func GetGlobalCacheStats() CacheStats {
        return globalCache.Stats()
}

package git

import (
        "fmt"
        "sync"
        "time"

        "github.com/collabops/git-executor/internal/cache"
        gogit "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5"
)

var (
        // globalRepoCache is the global repository cache instance
        globalRepoCache cache.RepositoryCache

        // globalCacheMutex protects initialization of the global cache
        globalCacheMutex sync.RWMutex

        // defaultCacheConfig is the default configuration for the repository cache
        defaultCacheConfig = &cache.CacheConfig{
                Enabled:         true,
                MaxRepositories: 100,
                TTL:             30 * time.Minute, // 30 minutes
                MaxMemoryMB:     512,              // 512MB max memory
                CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,  // 5 minutes cleanup
        }
)

// InitializeGlobalCache initializes the global repository cache with the given configuration
func InitializeGlobalCache(config *cache.CacheConfig) error {
        globalCacheMutex.Lock()
        defer globalCacheMutex.Unlock()

        if config == nil {
                config = defaultCacheConfig
        }

        repoCache, err := cache.NewRepositoryCache(config)
        if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize repository cache: %w", err)
        }

        // Close the old cache if it exists
        if globalRepoCache != nil {
                _ = globalRepoCache.Close()
        }

        globalRepoCache = repoCache
        return nil
}

// GetGlobalRepoCache returns the global repository cache instance
// If not initialized, it creates one with default configuration
func GetGlobalRepoCache() cache.RepositoryCache {
        globalCacheMutex.RLock()
        if globalRepoCache != nil {
                globalCacheMutex.RUnlock()
                return globalRepoCache
        }
        globalCacheMutex.RUnlock()

        // Initialize with default config if not already done
        globalCacheMutex.Lock()
        defer globalCacheMutex.Unlock()

        // Double-check after acquiring write lock
        if globalRepoCache != nil {
                return globalRepoCache
        }

        repoCache, err := cache.NewRepositoryCache(defaultCacheConfig)
        if err != nil {
                // If cache creation fails, create a disabled cache
                disabledConfig := &cache.CacheConfig{Enabled: false}
                repoCache, _ = cache.NewRepositoryCache(disabledConfig)
        }

        globalRepoCache = repoCache
        return globalRepoCache
}

// OpenRepositoryWithNewCache opens a Git repository using our new cache implementation
func OpenRepositoryWithNewCache(path string) (Repository, error) {
        cache := GetGlobalRepoCache()

        // Try to get from cache first
        if gitRepo, found := cache.GetRepository(path); found {
                // Check if the cached repository is still valid (not nil)
                if gitRepo != nil {
                        // Return a properly initialized GoGitRepository
                        return &GoGitRepository{
                                path: path,
                                repo: gitRepo,
                                mu:   sync.RWMutex{}, // Important: Initialize the mutex!
                        }, nil
                }
                // If gitRepo is nil, the repository was closed, so we'll re-open it below
        }

        // Not in cache or was closed, open the repository
        gitRepo, err := gogit.PlainOpen(path)
        if err != nil {
                if err == gogit.ErrRepositoryNotExists {
                        return nil, &InvalidRepositoryError{
                                Path:   path,
                                Reason: "directory is not a Git repository",
                        }
                }
                return nil, NewGitError("open", path, "", "failed to open repository", err)
        }

        // Store in cache
        if err := cache.SetRepository(path, gitRepo); err != nil {
                // Log cache error but don't fail the operation
                fmt.Printf("Warning: failed to cache repository %s: %v\n", path, err)
        }

        return &GoGitRepository{
                path: path,
                repo: gitRepo,
                mu:   sync.RWMutex{}, // Initialize the mutex!
        }, nil
}

// InvalidateCachedRepository removes a repository from the cache
// This should be called after repository modifications (e.g., push operations)
func InvalidateCachedRepository(path string) bool {
        cache := GetGlobalRepoCache()
        return cache.InvalidateRepository(path)
}

// InvalidateAllCachedRepositories clears the entire repository cache
func InvalidateAllCachedRepositories() {
        cache := GetGlobalRepoCache()
        cache.InvalidateAll()
}

// GetCacheMetrics returns metrics from the repository cache
func GetCacheMetrics() cache.CacheMetrics {
        cache := GetGlobalRepoCache()
        return cache.GetMetrics()
}

// ShutdownCache gracefully shuts down the repository cache
func ShutdownCache() error {
        globalCacheMutex.Lock()
        defer globalCacheMutex.Unlock()

        if globalRepoCache != nil {
                err := globalRepoCache.Close()
                globalRepoCache = nil
                return err
        }

        return nil
}

package git

import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "strings"
        "time"

        gogit "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5"
        "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing"
        "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/object"
        "go.uber.org/zap"

        "github.com/collabops/git-executor/internal/logging"
        "github.com/collabops/git-executor/internal/repository"
)

// ConflictDetector provides merge conflict detection and analysis capabilities
type ConflictDetector struct {
        pathConfig *repository.PathConfig
        logger     *logging.Logger
}

// NewConflictDetector creates a new conflict detector instance
func NewConflictDetector(pathConfig *repository.PathConfig, logger *logging.Logger) *ConflictDetector {
        return &ConflictDetector{
                pathConfig: pathConfig,
                logger:     logger,
        }
}

// ConflictType represents the type of merge conflict
type ConflictType string

const (
        ConflictTypeContent   ConflictType = "content"   // Content conflicts within file
        ConflictTypeRename    ConflictType = "rename"    // File renamed in both branches
        ConflictTypeDelete    ConflictType = "delete"    // File deleted in one branch, modified in other
        ConflictTypeAdd       ConflictType = "add"       // File added in both branches with different content
        ConflictTypeMode      ConflictType = "mode"      // File mode conflicts (permissions)
        ConflictTypeSubmodule ConflictType = "submodule" // Submodule conflicts
        ConflictTypeSymlink   ConflictType = "symlink"   // Symlink conflicts
)

// ConflictSeverity represents the severity level of a conflict
type ConflictSeverity string

const (
        ConflictSeverityLow      ConflictSeverity = "low"      // Easy to resolve automatically
        ConflictSeverityMedium   ConflictSeverity = "medium"   // Requires manual review
        ConflictSeverityHigh     ConflictSeverity = "high"     // Complex conflicts requiring careful resolution
        ConflictSeverityCritical ConflictSeverity = "critical" // Conflicts that may cause data loss if resolved incorrectly
)

// MergeStrategy represents different merge strategies
type MergeStrategy string

const (
        MergeStrategyRecursive MergeStrategy = "recursive" // Default three-way merge
        MergeStrategyResolve   MergeStrategy = "resolve"   // Three-way merge with aggressive resolution
        MergeStrategyOctopus   MergeStrategy = "octopus"   // Multi-branch merge
        MergeStrategyOurs      MergeStrategy = "ours"      // Keep our version on conflicts
        MergeStrategyTheirs    MergeStrategy = "theirs"    // Keep their version on conflicts
        MergeStrategySubtree   MergeStrategy = "subtree"   // Subtree merge strategy
)

// ConflictRegion represents a specific conflict within a file
type ConflictRegion struct {
        StartLine    int    `json:"start_line"`    // Starting line number of conflict
        EndLine      int    `json:"end_line"`      // Ending line number of conflict
        OurContent   string `json:"our_content"`   // Content from our branch
        TheirContent string `json:"their_content"` // Content from their branch
        BaseContent  string `json:"base_content"`  // Content from common ancestor
        MarkerStyle  string `json:"marker_style"`  // Conflict marker style (<<<, ===, >>>)
}

// FileConflict represents conflicts within a single file
type FileConflict struct {
        FilePath       string                 `json:"file_path"`            // Path to the conflicted file
        ConflictType   ConflictType           `json:"conflict_type"`        // Type of conflict
        Severity       ConflictSeverity       `json:"severity"`             // Conflict severity level
        OurVersion     *FileVersion           `json:"our_version"`          // Our branch version
        TheirVersion   *FileVersion           `json:"their_version"`        // Their branch version
        BaseVersion    *FileVersion           `json:"base_version"`         // Common ancestor version
        Regions        []ConflictRegion       `json:"regions"`              // Specific conflict regions
        AutoResolvable bool                   `json:"auto_resolvable"`      // Can be automatically resolved
        Resolution     *ConflictResolution    `json:"resolution,omitempty"` // Suggested resolution
        Metadata       map[string]interface{} `json:"metadata,omitempty"`   // Additional metadata
}

// FileVersion represents a version of a file at a specific commit
type FileVersion struct {
        Hash        plumbing.Hash `json:"hash"`              // Object hash
        Mode        uint32        `json:"mode"`              // File mode (permissions)
        Size        int64         `json:"size"`              // File size in bytes
        Content     string        `json:"content,omitempty"` // File content (for small files)
        ContentHash string        `json:"content_hash"`      // Hash of file content
        IsBinary    bool          `json:"is_binary"`         // Whether file is binary
        Exists      bool          `json:"exists"`            // Whether file exists in this version
}

// ConflictResolution represents a suggested resolution for a conflict
type ConflictResolution struct {
        Strategy     string                 `json:"strategy"`           // Resolution strategy
        Content      string                 `json:"content"`            // Resolved content
        Confidence   float64                `json:"confidence"`         // Confidence in resolution (0.0-1.0)
        AutoApplied  bool                   `json:"auto_applied"`       // Whether resolution was automatically applied
        Reasoning    string                 `json:"reasoning"`          // Explanation of resolution
        Alternatives []string               `json:"alternatives"`       // Alternative resolutions
        Metadata     map[string]interface{} `json:"metadata,omitempty"` // Additional metadata
}

// MergeAnalysisRequest represents a request for merge analysis
type MergeAnalysisRequest struct {
        Owner          string        `json:"owner"`           // Repository owner
        Repo           string        `json:"repo"`            // Repository name
        SourceRef      string        `json:"source_ref"`      // Source branch/commit to merge FROM
        TargetRef      string        `json:"target_ref"`      // Target branch/commit to merge INTO
        Strategy       MergeStrategy `json:"strategy"`        // Preferred merge strategy
        AutoResolve    bool          `json:"auto_resolve"`    // Whether to attempt automatic resolution
        IncludeContent bool          `json:"include_content"` // Whether to include file content in response
        MaxFileSize    int64         `json:"max_file_size"`   // Maximum file size to analyze for content conflicts
}

// MergeAnalysisResult represents the result of merge conflict analysis
type MergeAnalysisResult struct {
        CanMerge          bool                     `json:"can_merge"`          // Whether merge is possible
        HasConflicts      bool                     `json:"has_conflicts"`      // Whether conflicts exist
        IsFastForward     bool                     `json:"is_fast_forward"`    // Whether merge is fast-forward
        ConflictCount     int                      `json:"conflict_count"`     // Total number of conflicts
        FileConflicts     []FileConflict           `json:"file_conflicts"`     // Detailed file conflicts
        MergeBase         *MergeCommitInfo         `json:"merge_base"`         // Common ancestor commit
        SourceCommit      *MergeCommitInfo         `json:"source_commit"`      // Source commit info
        TargetCommit      *MergeCommitInfo         `json:"target_commit"`      // Target commit info
        Strategy          MergeStrategy            `json:"strategy"`           // Merge strategy used
        AutoResolvable    int                      `json:"auto_resolvable"`    // Number of auto-resolvable conflicts
        SeverityBreakdown map[ConflictSeverity]int `json:"severity_breakdown"` // Conflicts by severity
        EstimatedTime     time.Duration            `json:"estimated_time"`     // Estimated resolution time
        Recommendations   []string                 `json:"recommendations"`    // Resolution recommendations
        Metadata          map[string]interface{}   `json:"metadata,omitempty"` // Additional metadata
}

// MergeCommitInfo represents information about a commit (used in merge operations)
type MergeCommitInfo struct {
        SHA       string                 `json:"sha"`
        Message   string                 `json:"message"`
        Author    AuthorInfo             `json:"author"`
        Committer AuthorInfo             `json:"committer"`
        CreatedAt time.Time              `json:"created_at"`
        Parents   []string               `json:"parents"`
        TreeSHA   string                 `json:"tree_sha"`
        Metadata  map[string]interface{} `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
}

// AuthorInfo represents commit author information
type AuthorInfo struct {
        Name  string    `json:"name"`
        Email string    `json:"email"`
        Date  time.Time `json:"date"`
}

// AnalyzeMerge performs comprehensive merge conflict analysis
func (cd *ConflictDetector) AnalyzeMerge(ctx context.Context, req *MergeAnalysisRequest) (*MergeAnalysisResult, error) {
        cd.logger.Info("Starting merge conflict analysis",
                zap.String("owner", req.Owner),
                zap.String("repo", req.Repo),
                zap.String("source_ref", req.SourceRef),
                zap.String("target_ref", req.TargetRef),
                zap.String("strategy", string(req.Strategy)))

        // Open repository
        repoPath := cd.pathConfig.FormatRepoPath(req.Owner, req.Repo)
        repo, err := gogit.PlainOpen(repoPath)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
        }

        // Resolve source and target commits
        sourceCommit, err := cd.resolveCommit(repo, req.SourceRef)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve source ref %s: %w", req.SourceRef, err)
        }

        targetCommit, err := cd.resolveCommit(repo, req.TargetRef)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve target ref %s: %w", req.TargetRef, err)
        }

        cd.logger.Debug("Resolved commits",
                zap.String("source_commit", sourceCommit.Hash.String()),
                zap.String("target_commit", targetCommit.Hash.String()))

        // Check for fast-forward merge
        isFastForward, err := cd.isFastForwardMerge(repo, targetCommit, sourceCommit)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to check fast-forward merge: %w", err)
        }

        if isFastForward {
                cd.logger.Info("Fast-forward merge detected")
                return &MergeAnalysisResult{
                        CanMerge:          true,
                        HasConflicts:      false,
                        IsFastForward:     true,
                        ConflictCount:     0,
                        FileConflicts:     []FileConflict{},
                        SourceCommit:      cd.commitToInfo(sourceCommit),
                        TargetCommit:      cd.commitToInfo(targetCommit),
                        Strategy:          req.Strategy,
                        AutoResolvable:    0,
                        SeverityBreakdown: make(map[ConflictSeverity]int),
                        EstimatedTime:     0,
                        Recommendations:   []string{"Fast-forward merge - no conflicts expected"},
                }, nil
        }

        // Find merge base (common ancestor)
        mergeBase, err := cd.findMergeBase(repo, sourceCommit, targetCommit)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to find merge base: %w", err)
        }

        cd.logger.Debug("Found merge base", zap.String("merge_base", mergeBase.Hash.String()))

        // Perform three-way merge analysis
        conflicts, err := cd.analyzeThreeWayMerge(ctx, repo, mergeBase, sourceCommit, targetCommit, req)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to analyze three-way merge: %w", err)
        }

        // Calculate summary statistics
        result := &MergeAnalysisResult{
                CanMerge:          len(conflicts) == 0 || cd.allAutoResolvable(conflicts),
                HasConflicts:      len(conflicts) > 0,
                IsFastForward:     false,
                ConflictCount:     len(conflicts),
                FileConflicts:     conflicts,
                MergeBase:         cd.commitToInfo(mergeBase),
                SourceCommit:      cd.commitToInfo(sourceCommit),
                TargetCommit:      cd.commitToInfo(targetCommit),
                Strategy:          req.Strategy,
                AutoResolvable:    cd.countAutoResolvable(conflicts),
                SeverityBreakdown: cd.calculateSeverityBreakdown(conflicts),
                EstimatedTime:     cd.estimateResolutionTime(conflicts),
                Recommendations:   cd.generateRecommendations(conflicts, req.Strategy),
        }

        cd.logger.Info("Merge analysis completed",
                zap.Int("total_conflicts", result.ConflictCount),
                zap.Int("auto_resolvable", result.AutoResolvable),
                zap.Bool("can_merge", result.CanMerge),
                zap.Duration("estimated_time", result.EstimatedTime))

        return result, nil
}

// resolveCommit resolves a reference to a commit object
func (cd *ConflictDetector) resolveCommit(repo *gogit.Repository, ref string) (*object.Commit, error) {
        // Try to resolve as hash first
        if hash := plumbing.NewHash(ref); !hash.IsZero() {
                return repo.CommitObject(hash)
        }

        // Try to resolve as reference
        reference, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(ref), true)
        if err == nil {
                return repo.CommitObject(reference.Hash())
        }

        // Try with refs/heads/ prefix for branch names
        if !strings.HasPrefix(ref, "refs/") {
                branchRef := "refs/heads/" + ref
                reference, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(branchRef), true)
                if err == nil {
                        return repo.CommitObject(reference.Hash())
                }

                // Try with refs/tags/ prefix for tag names
                tagRef := "refs/tags/" + ref
                reference, err = repo.Reference(plumbing.ReferenceName(tagRef), true)
                if err == nil {
                        return repo.CommitObject(reference.Hash())
                }
        }

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to resolve reference: %s", ref)
}

// isFastForwardMerge checks if the merge can be fast-forwarded
func (cd *ConflictDetector) isFastForwardMerge(repo *gogit.Repository, base, head *object.Commit) (bool, error) {
        // Check if base is an ancestor of head
        isAncestor, err := base.IsAncestor(head)
        if err != nil {
                return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to check ancestry: %w", err)
        }
        return isAncestor, nil
}

// findMergeBase finds the common ancestor of two commits
func (cd *ConflictDetector) findMergeBase(repo *gogit.Repository, commit1, commit2 *object.Commit) (*object.Commit, error) {
        // Use go-git's merge base functionality
        bases, err := commit1.MergeBase(commit2)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to find merge base: %w", err)
        }

        if len(bases) == 0 {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("no common ancestor found")
        }

        // Return the first (most recent) common ancestor
        return bases[0], nil
}

// analyzeThreeWayMerge performs detailed three-way merge analysis
func (cd *ConflictDetector) analyzeThreeWayMerge(ctx context.Context, repo *gogit.Repository, base, source, target *object.Commit, req *MergeAnalysisRequest) ([]FileConflict, error) {
        var conflicts []FileConflict

        // Get trees for all three commits
        baseTree, err := base.Tree()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
        }

        sourceTree, err := source.Tree()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get source tree: %w", err)
        }

        targetTree, err := target.Tree()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get target tree: %w", err)
        }

        // Compare trees to find differences
        baseFiles := make(map[string]*object.TreeEntry)
        sourceFiles := make(map[string]*object.TreeEntry)
        targetFiles := make(map[string]*object.TreeEntry)

        // Collect all files from all trees
        err = cd.collectTreeFiles(baseTree, baseFiles)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to collect base tree files: %w", err)
        }

        err = cd.collectTreeFiles(sourceTree, sourceFiles)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to collect source tree files: %w", err)
        }

        err = cd.collectTreeFiles(targetTree, targetFiles)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to collect target tree files: %w", err)
        }

        // Find all unique file paths
        allPaths := make(map[string]bool)
        for path := range baseFiles {
                allPaths[path] = true
        }
        for path := range sourceFiles {
                allPaths[path] = true
        }
        for path := range targetFiles {
                allPaths[path] = true
        }

        // Analyze each file for conflicts
        for path := range allPaths {
                conflict, err := cd.analyzeFileConflict(ctx, repo, path, baseFiles[path], sourceFiles[path], targetFiles[path], req)
                if err != nil {
                        cd.logger.Warn("Failed to analyze file conflict", zap.String("path", path), zap.Error(err))
                        continue
                }

                if conflict != nil {
                        conflicts = append(conflicts, *conflict)
                }
        }

        return conflicts, nil
}

// collectTreeFiles recursively collects all files from a tree
func (cd *ConflictDetector) collectTreeFiles(tree *object.Tree, files map[string]*object.TreeEntry) error {
        return tree.Files().ForEach(func(file *object.File) error {
                files[file.Name] = &object.TreeEntry{
                        Name: file.Name,
                        Mode: file.Mode,
                        Hash: file.Hash,
                }
                return nil
        })
}

// analyzeFileConflict analyzes a single file for conflicts
func (cd *ConflictDetector) analyzeFileConflict(ctx context.Context, repo *gogit.Repository, path string, base, source, target *object.TreeEntry, req *MergeAnalysisRequest) (*FileConflict, error) {
        // Determine file existence in each version
        baseExists := base != nil
        sourceExists := source != nil
        targetExists := target != nil

        // No conflict if file is unchanged
        if baseExists && sourceExists && targetExists &&
                base.Hash == source.Hash && base.Hash == target.Hash {
                return nil, nil
        }

        // Analyze conflict type and create file versions
        baseVersion := cd.createFileVersion(repo, base)
        sourceVersion := cd.createFileVersion(repo, source)
        targetVersion := cd.createFileVersion(repo, target)

        conflict := &FileConflict{
                FilePath:     path,
                OurVersion:   sourceVersion,
                TheirVersion: targetVersion,
                BaseVersion:  baseVersion,
                Regions:      []ConflictRegion{},
                Metadata:     make(map[string]interface{}),
        }

        // Determine conflict type
        conflict.ConflictType = cd.determineConflictType(baseExists, sourceExists, targetExists, base, source, target)
        conflict.Severity = cd.calculateConflictSeverity(conflict.ConflictType, sourceVersion, targetVersion)

        // Analyze content conflicts for text files
        if req.IncludeContent && conflict.ConflictType == ConflictTypeContent {
                regions, err := cd.analyzeContentConflicts(repo, base, source, target, req.MaxFileSize)
                if err != nil {
                        cd.logger.Warn("Failed to analyze content conflicts", zap.String("path", path), zap.Error(err))
                } else {
                        conflict.Regions = regions
                }
        }

        // Determine if auto-resolvable
        conflict.AutoResolvable = cd.isAutoResolvable(conflict)

        // Generate resolution suggestion if auto-resolvable
        if conflict.AutoResolvable && req.AutoResolve {
                resolution := cd.generateResolution(conflict)
                conflict.Resolution = resolution
        }

        return conflict, nil
}

// Helper methods for conflict analysis
func (cd *ConflictDetector) createFileVersion(repo *gogit.Repository, entry *object.TreeEntry) *FileVersion {
        if entry == nil {
                return &FileVersion{Exists: false}
        }

        version := &FileVersion{
                Hash:   entry.Hash,
                Mode:   uint32(entry.Mode),
                Exists: true,
        }

        // Get file object to determine additional properties
        if obj, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash); err == nil {
                version.Size = obj.Size
                version.ContentHash = obj.Hash.String()

                // Check if binary (simple heuristic)
                if reader, err := obj.Reader(); err == nil {
                        defer func() {
                                if err := reader.Close(); err != nil {
                                        // Log close error but don't return it since we're in cleanup
                                        fmt.Printf("Warning: failed to close reader during cleanup: %v\n", err)
                                }
                        }()
                        buffer := make([]byte, 512)
                        if n, err := reader.Read(buffer); err == nil {
                                version.IsBinary = cd.isBinaryContent(buffer[:n])
                        }
                }
        }

        return version
}

// determineConflictType determines the type of conflict based on file states
func (cd *ConflictDetector) determineConflictType(baseExists, sourceExists, targetExists bool, base, source, target *object.TreeEntry) ConflictType {
        // File deleted in one branch, modified in other
        if baseExists && !sourceExists && targetExists {
                // Check if base and target have different hashes (indicating modification)
                if base != nil && target != nil && base.Hash != target.Hash {
                        return ConflictTypeDelete
                } else if base == nil || target == nil {
                        // If we don't have tree entries but have existence flags, assume it's a delete conflict
                        return ConflictTypeDelete
                }
        }
        if baseExists && sourceExists && !targetExists {
                // Check if base and source have different hashes (indicating modification)
                if base != nil && source != nil && base.Hash != source.Hash {
                        return ConflictTypeDelete
                } else if base == nil || source == nil {
                        // If we don't have tree entries but have existence flags, assume it's a delete conflict
                        return ConflictTypeDelete
                }
        }

        // File added in both branches
        if !baseExists && sourceExists && targetExists {
                if source != nil && target != nil && source.Hash != target.Hash {
                        return ConflictTypeAdd
                } else if source == nil || target == nil {
                        // If we don't have tree entries but both exist, assume it's an add conflict
                        return ConflictTypeAdd
                }
        }

        // Mode conflicts
        if sourceExists && targetExists && source != nil && target != nil && source.Hash == target.Hash && source.Mode != target.Mode {
                return ConflictTypeMode
        }

        // Content conflicts (most common)
        if sourceExists && targetExists && source != nil && target != nil && source.Hash != target.Hash {
                return ConflictTypeContent
        }

        // Default fallback
        return ConflictTypeContent
}

// calculateConflictSeverity determines the severity of a conflict
func (cd *ConflictDetector) calculateConflictSeverity(conflictType ConflictType, sourceVersion, targetVersion *FileVersion) ConflictSeverity {
        switch conflictType {
        case ConflictTypeMode:
                return ConflictSeverityLow
        case ConflictTypeAdd:
                if sourceVersion != nil && targetVersion != nil && sourceVersion.IsBinary != targetVersion.IsBinary {
                        return ConflictSeverityHigh
                }
                return ConflictSeverityMedium
        case ConflictTypeDelete:
                return ConflictSeverityHigh
        case ConflictTypeContent:
                if (sourceVersion != nil && sourceVersion.IsBinary) || (targetVersion != nil && targetVersion.IsBinary) {
                        return ConflictSeverityCritical
                }
                return ConflictSeverityMedium
        default:
                return ConflictSeverityMedium
        }
}

// analyzeContentConflicts analyzes content-level conflicts within a file
func (cd *ConflictDetector) analyzeContentConflicts(repo *gogit.Repository, base, source, target *object.TreeEntry, maxFileSize int64) ([]ConflictRegion, error) {
        // This is a simplified implementation - in practice, you'd want more sophisticated
        // three-way merge analysis using libraries like go-git's merge package
        var regions []ConflictRegion

        // Get file contents
        baseContent, err := cd.getFileContent(repo, base, maxFileSize)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base content: %w", err)
        }

        sourceContent, err := cd.getFileContent(repo, source, maxFileSize)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get source content: %w", err)
        }

        targetContent, err := cd.getFileContent(repo, target, maxFileSize)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get target content: %w", err)
        }

        // Simple line-based conflict detection
        baseLines := strings.Split(baseContent, "\n")
        sourceLines := strings.Split(sourceContent, "\n")
        targetLines := strings.Split(targetContent, "\n")

        // This is a simplified algorithm - real implementation would use
        // Myers diff algorithm or similar for accurate three-way merge
        if len(sourceLines) != len(targetLines) || strings.Join(sourceLines, "\n") != strings.Join(targetLines, "\n") {
                regions = append(regions, ConflictRegion{
                        StartLine:    1,
                        EndLine:      len(sourceLines),
                        OurContent:   strings.Join(sourceLines, "\n"),
                        TheirContent: strings.Join(targetLines, "\n"),
                        BaseContent:  strings.Join(baseLines, "\n"),
                        MarkerStyle:  "standard",
                })
        }

        return regions, nil
}

// Helper methods
func (cd *ConflictDetector) getFileContent(repo *gogit.Repository, entry *object.TreeEntry, maxFileSize int64) (string, error) {
        if entry == nil {
                return "", nil
        }

        obj, err := repo.BlobObject(entry.Hash)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }

        if obj.Size > maxFileSize {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("file too large: %d bytes", obj.Size)
        }

        reader, err := obj.Reader()
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        defer func() {
                if err := reader.Close(); err != nil {
                        // Log close error during cleanup - not critical
                        fmt.Printf("Warning: failed to close reader during cleanup: %v\n", err)
                }
        }()

        content := make([]byte, obj.Size)
        _, err = reader.Read(content)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }

        return string(content), nil
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) isBinaryContent(data []byte) bool {
        // Simple binary detection - check for null bytes
        for _, b := range data {
                if b == 0 {
                        return true
                }
        }
        return false
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) isAutoResolvable(conflict *FileConflict) bool {
        switch conflict.ConflictType {
        case ConflictTypeMode:
                return true // Mode conflicts are often auto-resolvable
        case ConflictTypeAdd:
                return false // Adding same file with different content needs manual review
        case ConflictTypeDelete:
                return false // Delete conflicts need manual review
        case ConflictTypeContent:
                return len(conflict.Regions) == 0 || (conflict.OurVersion != nil && !conflict.OurVersion.IsBinary && conflict.TheirVersion != nil && !conflict.TheirVersion.IsBinary)
        default:
                return false
        }
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) generateResolution(conflict *FileConflict) *ConflictResolution {
        switch conflict.ConflictType {
        case ConflictTypeMode:
                // For mode conflicts, typically choose the more permissive mode
                return &ConflictResolution{
                        Strategy:   "prefer_permissive_mode",
                        Confidence: 0.8,
                        Reasoning:  "Mode conflicts resolved by choosing more permissive file mode",
                }
        default:
                return &ConflictResolution{
                        Strategy:   "manual_review_required",
                        Confidence: 0.0,
                        Reasoning:  "This conflict requires manual review and resolution",
                }
        }
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) allAutoResolvable(conflicts []FileConflict) bool {
        for _, conflict := range conflicts {
                if !conflict.AutoResolvable {
                        return false
                }
        }
        return true
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) countAutoResolvable(conflicts []FileConflict) int {
        count := 0
        for _, conflict := range conflicts {
                if conflict.AutoResolvable {
                        count++
                }
        }
        return count
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) calculateSeverityBreakdown(conflicts []FileConflict) map[ConflictSeverity]int {
        breakdown := make(map[ConflictSeverity]int)
        for _, conflict := range conflicts {
                breakdown[conflict.Severity]++
        }
        return breakdown
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) estimateResolutionTime(conflicts []FileConflict) time.Duration {
        var totalMinutes int
        for _, conflict := range conflicts {
                switch conflict.Severity {
                case ConflictSeverityLow:
                        totalMinutes += 2
                case ConflictSeverityMedium:
                        totalMinutes += 10
                case ConflictSeverityHigh:
                        totalMinutes += 30
                case ConflictSeverityCritical:
                        totalMinutes += 60
                }
        }
        return time.Duration(totalMinutes) * time.Minute
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) generateRecommendations(conflicts []FileConflict, strategy MergeStrategy) []string {
        var recommendations []string

        if len(conflicts) == 0 {
                return []string{"No conflicts detected - merge can proceed safely"}
        }

        autoResolvable := cd.countAutoResolvable(conflicts)
        if autoResolvable == len(conflicts) {
                recommendations = append(recommendations, "All conflicts can be automatically resolved")
        } else {
                recommendations = append(recommendations, fmt.Sprintf("%d of %d conflicts require manual resolution", len(conflicts)-autoResolvable, len(conflicts)))
        }

        // Strategy-specific recommendations
        switch strategy {
        case MergeStrategyRecursive:
                recommendations = append(recommendations, "Recursive strategy provides good conflict detection")
        case MergeStrategyOurs:
                recommendations = append(recommendations, "Using 'ours' strategy will favor your changes in conflicts")
        case MergeStrategyTheirs:
                recommendations = append(recommendations, "Using 'theirs' strategy will favor their changes in conflicts")
        }

        return recommendations
}

func (cd *ConflictDetector) commitToInfo(commit *object.Commit) *MergeCommitInfo {
        parents := make([]string, len(commit.ParentHashes))
        for i, hash := range commit.ParentHashes {
                parents[i] = hash.String()
        }

        return &MergeCommitInfo{
                SHA:       commit.Hash.String(),
                Message:   commit.Message,
                Author:    AuthorInfo{Name: commit.Author.Name, Email: commit.Author.Email, Date: commit.Author.When},
                Committer: AuthorInfo{Name: commit.Committer.Name, Email: commit.Committer.Email, Date: commit.Committer.When},
                CreatedAt: commit.Author.When,
                Parents:   parents,
                TreeSHA:   commit.TreeHash.String(),
        }
}

package git

import (
        "fmt"
)

// GitError represents errors that occur during Git operations
type GitError struct {
        // Operation is the Git operation that failed
        Operation string

        // Path is the repository or file path involved
        Path string

        // Ref is the Git reference (branch, tag, commit) if applicable
        Ref string

        // Message is the error message
        Message string

        // Err is the underlying error
        Err error
}

// Error implements the error interface
func (e *GitError) Error() string {
        if e.Ref != "" {
                return fmt.Sprintf("git %s failed for path %q at ref %q: %s", e.Operation, e.Path, e.Ref, e.Message)
        }
        return fmt.Sprintf("git %s failed for path %q: %s", e.Operation, e.Path, e.Message)
}

// Unwrap returns the underlying error
func (e *GitError) Unwrap() error {
        return e.Err
}

// NewGitError creates a new GitError
func NewGitError(operation, path, ref, message string, err error) *GitError {
        return &GitError{
                Operation: operation,
                Path:      path,
                Ref:       ref,
                Message:   message,
                Err:       err,
        }
}

// RepositoryNotFoundError indicates that a repository was not found
type RepositoryNotFoundError struct {
        Path string
}

// Error implements the error interface
func (e *RepositoryNotFoundError) Error() string {
        return fmt.Sprintf("repository not found at path: %s", e.Path)
}

// ReferenceNotFoundError indicates that a Git reference was not found
type ReferenceNotFoundError struct {
        Ref  string
        Path string
}

// Error implements the error interface
func (e *ReferenceNotFoundError) Error() string {
        return fmt.Sprintf("reference %q not found in repository at %s", e.Ref, e.Path)
}

// PathNotFoundError indicates that a path was not found in a Git tree
type PathNotFoundError struct {
        Path string
        Ref  string
        Repo string
}

// Error implements the error interface
func (e *PathNotFoundError) Error() string {
        return fmt.Sprintf("path %q not found at ref %q in repository %s", e.Path, e.Ref, e.Repo)
}

// InvalidRepositoryError indicates that a directory is not a valid Git repository
type InvalidRepositoryError struct {
        Path   string
        Reason string
}

// Error implements the error interface
func (e *InvalidRepositoryError) Error() string {
        return fmt.Sprintf("invalid repository at %s: %s", e.Path, e.Reason)
}

package git

import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing"
        "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/filemode"
        "github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/object"
        "go.uber.org/zap"
)

// SingleFileOperation represents a single file operation request
type SingleFileOperation struct {
        // Repository information
        Owner string `json:"owner"`
        Repo  string `json:"repo"`

        // File information
        Path    string `json:"path"`
        Content []byte `json:"content"`

        // Commit information
        Message        string `json:"message"`
        AuthorName     string `json:"author_name"`
        AuthorEmail    string `json:"author_email"`
        CommitterName  string `json:"committer_name,omitempty"`
        CommitterEmail string `json:"committer_email,omitempty"`

        // Git information
        Branch string `json:"branch"`
}

// MultiFileOperation represents a multi-file operation request
type MultiFileOperation struct {
        // Repository information
        Owner string `json:"owner"`
        Repo  string `json:"repo"`

        // File changes
        Changes []FileChange `json:"changes"`

        // Commit information
        Message        string `json:"message"`
        AuthorName     string `json:"author_name"`
        AuthorEmail    string `json:"author_email"`
        CommitterName  string `json:"committer_name,omitempty"`
        CommitterEmail string `json:"committer_email,omitempty"`

        // Git information
        Branch string `json:"branch"`
}

// FileOperationResult represents the result of a file operation
type FileOperationResult struct {
        // Operation results
        CommitHash string `json:"commit_hash"`
        TreeHash   string `json:"tree_hash"`

        // File tracking
        ChangedFiles []string `json:"changed_files,omitempty"`
        CreatedFiles []string `json:"created_files,omitempty"`
        DeletedFiles []string `json:"deleted_files,omitempty"`

        // Commit metadata
        Message   string    `json:"message"`
        Author    string    `json:"author"`
        Timestamp time.Time `json:"timestamp"`
}

// CreateSingleFile creates a new file in the repository
func (gom *GitObjectManager) CreateSingleFile(ctx context.Context, operation SingleFileOperation) (*FileOperationResult, error) {
        gom.logger.Info("Creating single file",
                zap.String("owner", operation.Owner),
                zap.String("repo", operation.Repo),
                zap.String("path", operation.Path),
                zap.String("branch", operation.Branch))

        // Open repository
        repo, err := gom.OpenRepository(ctx, operation.Owner, operation.Repo)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open repository: %w", err)
        }

        // Get current HEAD or branch
        var baseCommitHash plumbing.Hash
        if operation.Branch != "" {
                baseCommitHash, err = gom.ResolveReference(ctx, repo, "refs/heads/"+operation.Branch)
                if err != nil {
                        // Branch doesn't exist, get HEAD
                        headRef, headErr := gom.GetRepositoryHead(ctx, repo)
                        if headErr != nil {
                                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve branch %s and HEAD: %w", operation.Branch, headErr)
                        }
                        baseCommitHash = headRef.Hash()
                }
        } else {
                headRef, err := gom.GetRepositoryHead(ctx, repo)
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get repository HEAD: %w", err)
                }
                baseCommitHash = headRef.Hash()
        }

        // Get base tree from current commit
        var baseTree *object.Tree
        if !baseCommitHash.IsZero() {
                baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(baseCommitHash)
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base commit: %w", err)
                }
                baseTree, err = baseCommit.Tree()
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
                }
        }

        // Create file change
        changes := []FileChange{
                {
                        Path:      operation.Path,
                        Operation: FileOperationCreate,
                        Content:   operation.Content,
                },
        }

        // Validate changes
        if err := gom.ValidateFileChanges(ctx, changes); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("file validation failed: %w", err)
        }

        // Create new tree
        treeResult, err := gom.CreateTreeFromChanges(ctx, repo, baseTree, changes)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create tree: %w", err)
        }

        // Prepare commit info
        commitInfo := CommitInfo{
                Message: operation.Message,
                Author: object.Signature{
                        Name:  operation.AuthorName,
                        Email: operation.AuthorEmail,
                        When:  time.Now(),
                },
        }

        // Set committer if provided
        if operation.CommitterName != "" && operation.CommitterEmail != "" {
                commitInfo.Committer = &object.Signature{
                        Name:  operation.CommitterName,
                        Email: operation.CommitterEmail,
                        When:  time.Now(),
                }
        }

        // Add parent if we have a base commit
        if !baseCommitHash.IsZero() {
                commitInfo.Parents = []plumbing.Hash{baseCommitHash}
        }

        // Create commit
        commitResult, err := gom.CreateCommit(ctx, repo, treeResult.TreeHash, commitInfo)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create commit: %w", err)
        }

        // Update branch reference if specified
        if operation.Branch != "" {
                refName := plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/heads/" + operation.Branch)
                ref := plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, commitResult.Hash)
                if err := repo.Storer.SetReference(ref); err != nil {
                        gom.logger.Warn("Failed to update branch reference",
                                zap.String("branch", operation.Branch),
                                zap.Error(err))
                }
        }

        return &FileOperationResult{
                CommitHash:   commitResult.Hash.String(),
                TreeHash:     commitResult.TreeHash.String(),
                CreatedFiles: treeResult.CreatedFiles,
                ChangedFiles: treeResult.ChangedFiles,
                DeletedFiles: treeResult.DeletedFiles,
                Message:      commitResult.Message,
                Author:       commitResult.Author.Name,
                Timestamp:    commitResult.Author.When,
        }, nil
}

// UpdateSingleFile updates an existing file in the repository
func (gom *GitObjectManager) UpdateSingleFile(ctx context.Context, operation SingleFileOperation) (*FileOperationResult, error) {
        gom.logger.Info("Updating single file",
                zap.String("owner", operation.Owner),
                zap.String("repo", operation.Repo),
                zap.String("path", operation.Path),
                zap.String("branch", operation.Branch))

        // Use the same logic as CreateSingleFile but with update operation
        return gom.executeSingleFileOperation(ctx, operation, FileOperationUpdate)
}

// DeleteSingleFile deletes a file from the repository
func (gom *GitObjectManager) DeleteSingleFile(ctx context.Context, operation SingleFileOperation) (*FileOperationResult, error) {
        gom.logger.Info("Deleting single file",
                zap.String("owner", operation.Owner),
                zap.String("repo", operation.Repo),
                zap.String("path", operation.Path),
